instructions: Pat the roast dry. Rub it all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the roast for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until deep brown all over. Transfer it to a slow cooker.
Pour 1/4 cup of the broth into the hot skillet and scrape up the browned bits. Pour it into the slow cooker.
Slice the onions and mince the garlic. Add them to the slow cooker with the rest of the broth, the Worcestershire and the rosemary.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours or on high for 4 hours, until the beef shreds with a fork. Keep the lid on while it cooks.
Transfer the roast to a cutting board and let it rest for 15 minutes. Spoon the fat off the top of the juices and take out the rosemary.
Shred or thinly slice the beef and put it back in the juices to keep warm. Taste the juices. If they're flat, add a pinch more salt.
Heat the broiler. Split the rolls and brush the cut sides with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Broil, cut side up, for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden.
Pile the beef on the rolls. Serve with the juices in small bowls for dipping.
Leftover beef keeps in its juices in the fridge for 4 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pot over low heat.
method_notes: Lead is Spend With Pennies (4.98 from 239). It sears the roast, then cooks it 4 hours on high or 8 on low in beef broth, condensed French onion soup, beer, onion, garlic, rosemary and Worcestershire, and serves it on buttered, broiled rolls. Adapted for dairy-free: the butter on the rolls is olive oil, and the condensed soup and beer became more broth and a second onion, with a little more Worcestershire; there is no cheese. Scaled to 2 lb of beef and 4 rolls. Carlsbad Cravings is similar with soy sauce and cola and provolone. About 40 minutes of the time is hands on; the rest is the slow cooker.
